mainTopic: A wife's קונם on her work, and the household tasks a wife does for her husband
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about how a woman's קונם on her work can take effect, when her husband has rights to that work. רב שישא בריה דרב אידי and then רב אשי reject two comparisons to a mortgaged field, because a woman can never free herself from her marriage. רב אשי answers instead that a קונם is קדושת הגוף, and as רבא taught, הקדש cancels a שיעבוד. Still, the רבנן strengthened the husband's rights, so the קונם only takes effect after the marriage ends. A new משנה then lists the jobs a wife does for her husband and explains how maidservants she brings into the marriage reduce them. רבי אליעזר and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל stress that total idleness is harmful. The גמרא explains how a woman 'grinds' and notes that the משנה does not follow רבי חייא. It then concludes that the משנה's rule that a wife nurses her child does not follow בית שמאי. The amud ends by quoting the ברייתא's phrase 'if the baby recognized her,' which the discussion takes up next.

steps.title: The mortgaged field comparison
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of the earlier answer: the woman's case is like someone who says, 'This field I mortgaged to you will be consecrated once I redeem it,' and the הקדש takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like someone who says: 'This field that I mortgaged to you, when I redeem it from you, let it be consecrated.' The law is that it becomes consecrated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer that started before this section. It compares the woman's קונם on her work to consecrating a mortgaged field 'for when I redeem it.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mortgaged field still belongs to its owner, even though the lender has rights to it right now. So the owner can set up a הקדש that kicks in once the lender's rights end. The idea is that the woman's work is the same: her husband has rights to it now, but it is still hers underneath.

keyTerms.meaning: I mortgaged (gave as security for a loan)
When I redeem it (pay off the loan and take it back)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new case appearing out of nowhere. It is the end of a comparison the גמרא started earlier, to explain how a woman's קונם can work.

phrases.english: "This field that I mortgaged to you,
when I redeem it from you, let it be consecrated",
where the law is that it is consecrated.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׂדֶה זוֹ שֶׁמִּשְׁכַּנְתִּי לְךָ, לִכְשֶׁאֶפְדֶּנָּה מִמְּךָ — תִּיקְדַּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an analogy the גמרא began before this section.
steps.terutzMaskana: A קונם on something owned but currently tied up by someone else's rights can take effect for later, like a mortgaged field.

steps.title: The field owner can redeem, but the woman cannot divorce herself
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי attacks the comparison: the field owner can end the mortgage whenever he wants, but a woman has no power to end her marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא son of רב אידי objected: Are the cases really alike? There, the owner can redeem the field whenever he wants. Here, the woman cannot divorce herself!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא challenges the comparison from step 1. He points out a big difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the field, the owner controls when the lender's rights end, because he can pay back the loan at any time. With the woman, only the husband can give a גט, so she has no control over when his rights to her work end. That makes the comparison weak.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it (a strong challenge)
Is it comparable? (Are the cases really alike?)
It is in his power, under his control

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, objects to this:
Is it comparable?
There, it is in his power to redeem it.
Here, it is not in her power to divorce herself!
phrases.notes: "Here" means the woman who made a קונם on her work.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי: מִי דָּמֵי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the analogy in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between the woman's קונם and the mortgaged field
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The field owner controls when the lender's rights end, but the woman has no control over when her husband's rights end.

steps.title: A better comparison: a field mortgaged for ten years
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא offers a closer comparison: a field mortgaged for a fixed ten years, which the owner cannot redeem early, and yet the הקדש still takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is only comparable to someone who tells his friend: 'This field that I mortgaged to you for ten years, when I redeem it from you, let it be consecrated.' The law is that it becomes consecrated.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after his objection, רב שישא swaps in a better comparison that fixes the problem he raised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a ten-year mortgage the owner cannot take the field back early, so he has no control right now, just like the woman. Even so, the הקדש takes effect once the field returns to him. The same logic means the woman's קונם can work for whenever her work comes back to her, for example if she is divorced.
steps.confusionAlert: רב שישא is not throwing out the whole idea. He keeps the same basic answer and only replaces the comparison with a closer one.

phrases.english: This is only comparable
to one who says to his fellow:
"This field that I mortgaged to you for ten years,
phrases.notes: A ten-year mortgage means the owner can't buy the field back early, just like she can't leave the marriage.

phrases.english: when I redeem it from you, let it be consecrated",
where the law is that it is consecrated.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא דָּמְיָא אֶלָּא לָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the analogy that was attacked in step 2 with a closer one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The woman's case is like a field the owner can redeem at any time.
steps.terutzMaskana: The woman's case is like a field locked in a mortgage for ten years, which still becomes הקדש once it returns.

steps.title: After ten years he can redeem, but she can never free herself
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects the ten-year comparison: the field owner will at least be able to redeem after ten years, while a woman can never divorce herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objected: Are the cases really alike? There, after ten years at least, he will be able to redeem it. Here, she will never be able to divorce herself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks רב שישא's new comparison from step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ten-year owner loses control only for a while, and after ten years he will surely be able to redeem. The woman can never end the marriage herself, at any point. So even the improved comparison doesn't fit.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: מִי דָּמֵי?
phrases.english: Rav Ashi objects to this: Is it comparable?
There, after ten years at least,
it is in his power to redeem it.
Here, it is not in her power
to divorce herself, ever.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: מִי דָּמֵי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the improved analogy from step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The field owner will surely be able to redeem after ten years, but the woman never gets the power to free herself, so the cases are not alike.

steps.title: A new answer: קונמות are קדושת הגוף
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי drops the mortgage comparisons entirely and explains that a קונם is a kind of built-in holiness, so it can take effect even on something her husband has rights to.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: You are talking about קונמות? קונמות are different, because they are קדושת הגוף, built-in holiness of the item itself.
steps.whatsHappening: Since both comparisons failed, רב אשי gives a completely different answer. A קונם is a strong kind of holiness that can override someone else's rights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier approach said the קונם works only later, once the husband's rights end. רב אשי says it works because a קונם is קדושת הגוף, a holiness that sits on the item itself. That kind of holiness is strong enough to push aside the husband's rights.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (we drop the earlier approach and give a new one)
Vows that forbid something as if it were הקדש
Holiness on the item itself, not just on its money value

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes how the whole question gets solved. We no longer need a mortgage comparison: a קונם is the kind of holiness that can take hold on property someone else has rights to. Steps 7-8 explain why it still waits until the marriage ends.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Are you talking about konamot?
Konamot are different,
since they are inherent sanctity,
phrases.notes: He means the holiness takes hold of the object itself, not just its money value.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: קוּנָּמוֹת קָא אָמְרַתְּ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the mortgage comparisons fail, gives an entirely new explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the category (קונם as קדושת הגוף)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A קונם works like ordinary הקדש on mortgaged property, taking effect only once the other person's rights end.
steps.terutzMaskana: A קונם is קדושת הגוף, and that strength lets it override the husband's rights.

steps.title: רבא's rule: הקדש, חמץ and שחרור cancel a lien
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי backs up his answer with רבא's rule that הקדש, חמץ on פסח, and freeing a slave all cancel a שיעבוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like רבא's view, since רבא said: הקדש, חמץ, and שחרור (freeing a slave) cancel a lien.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי supports his new answer with a known rule of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא teaches that certain strong forces wipe out another person's rights on property: הקדש, the איסור of חמץ, and freeing a slave. Since a קונם is a type of הקדש with קדושת הגוף, it also wipes out the husband's rights to her work.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrating property to the בית המקדש
A lien, someone else's legal claim on property

steps.whatToRemember: Two mortgage comparisons failed, because a woman can never free herself from marriage. רב אשי's answer is that a קונם is קדושת הגוף, and like רבא said, הקדש cancels a שיעבוד, so in principle her קונם can take hold even though her husband has rights to her work. The next step asks why it then doesn't take effect right away.

phrases.english: And this is in line with Rava.
As Rava said:
Consecration, leavened bread, and liberation of a slave
phrases.notes: חמץ here means once פסח comes, the חמץ becomes forbidden even if someone else had a claim on it.

phrases.english: cancel a lien.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אשי's answer in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That a קונם can take effect on a woman's work even though her husband has rights to it
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא: הקדש, חמץ and שחרור cancel a שיעבוד

steps.title: Then Let the קונם Take Effect Right Now
steps.stepSummary: If a קונם can cancel a שיעבוד, the woman's earnings should become forbidden immediately, not only after a divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let her earnings become holy right now!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes רב אשי's idea one step further. If a קונם is strong enough to cancel the husband's rights, it should work right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion assumed the קונם only takes effect later, after a divorce. But רב אשי (backed by רבא) said holiness cancels a שיעבוד. If so, why wait? The husband's rights should not hold it back even now.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow that makes something forbidden like a קרבן

phrases.english: Then let them become holy from now!
phrases.notes: 'Them' means her earnings, which she forbade to her husband with a קונם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב אשי's rule (that holiness cancels a שיעבוד) to ask why the קונם is delayed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the קונם only takes effect after divorce.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If holiness overrides the husband's rights, nothing should stop the קונם from working immediately.

steps.title: The Sages Strengthened the Husband's Rights
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן made the husband's rights to her earnings extra strong, so the קונם cannot take effect while they are married.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages strengthened the husband's lien, so that her earnings would not become holy right now.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן gave the husband's rights extra strength. So the קונם waits until those rights end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the basic rule, holiness would beat the husband's שיעבוד. But the husband's rights to his wife's earnings come from the רבנן, and they made those rights stronger than an ordinary lien. So during the marriage the קונם is blocked, and it only takes effect if she leaves the marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: A lien; a legal right someone has on property

steps.whatToRemember: A קונם on a wife's earnings can take effect after a divorce, but not during the marriage, because the רבנן strengthened the husband's rights.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the husband should annul the vow (in case of a future divorce), even though it does nothing to him right now.

phrases.english: The Sages strengthened the husband's lien,
so that it should not become holy from now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic strengthening of the husband's rights
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Holiness should override the husband's lien immediately.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן made the husband's lien extra strong, so the קונם waits until after divorce.

steps.title: The Tasks a Wife Does for Her Husband
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists seven jobs a wife does in the home.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the jobs a wife does for her husband: she grinds grain, bakes, washes clothes, cooks, nurses her child, makes his bed, and works with wool.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists the basic household jobs that a wife takes on in marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic. Just as the husband has duties to his wife, the משנה lists her duties in the home. The next part of the משנה will explain how these jobs shrink if she brings maidservants into the marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: She works with wool (spinning it into thread)

phrases.english: MISHNAH: And these are the tasks
that a wife does for her husband:
she grinds, and bakes, and washes clothes, cooks,
and nurses her child,
makes the bed for him, and works with wool.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wife does seven household tasks: grinding, baking, washing, cooking, nursing, making the bed, and working wool.

steps.title: Maidservants Lighten Her Load
steps.stepSummary: For each maidservant she brings into the marriage, the wife is excused from more of the tasks. With four, she does nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she brought one maidservant, she does not grind, bake, or wash. With two, she does not cook or nurse. With three, she does not make the bed or work wool. With four, she sits in an armchair.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains that the maidservants a wife brings from home take over her jobs, step by step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The jobs are dropped in order, starting with the hardest. One maidservant takes the heavy work, two take cooking and nursing, three take the personal tasks. With four, the wife is like a queen and does no housework at all.

keyTerms.meaning: She brought into the marriage for him
An armchair, a seat of honor

steps.confusionAlert: 'Brought' means she brought the maidservant from her own family into the marriage. It is not about servants the husband already owns.

phrases.english: If she brought him one maidservant,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא טוֹחֶנֶת וְלֹא אוֹפָה וְלֹא מְכַבֶּסֶת.
phrases.english: she does not grind, and does not bake, and does not wash clothes.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתַּיִם — אֵין מְבַשֶּׁלֶת, וְאֵין מְנִיקָה אֶת בְּנָהּ.
phrases.english: Two: she does not cook, and does not nurse her child.
Three: she does not make the bed for him,
and does not work with wool.
Four: she sits in an armchair.
phrases.notes: Sitting in the armchair means she lives like a lady and does no housework at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds when the wife is excused from the tasks listed in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each maidservant she brings excuses the wife from more tasks. With four she is excused from all of them.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: She Must Always Work With Wool
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says that even with a hundred maidservants, the husband can make her work with wool, because idleness leads to immoral behavior.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: Even if she brought him a hundred maidservants, he can force her to work with wool, because doing nothing leads to immoral behavior.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר disagrees with the end of the משנה. He says a wife can never be completely free of work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said four maidservants free her from everything. רבי אליעזר says one job, working wool, always stays, no matter how many servants she has. His reason is moral: an idle person is drawn toward sinful behavior.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Even if she brought him a hundred maidservants,
he forces her to work with wool,
because idleness leads to immoral behavior.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר אֲפִילּוּ הִכְנִיסָה לוֹ מֵאָה שְׁפָחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ruling that four maidservants free her from all work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wife can always be made to work with wool, because idleness leads to immoral behavior.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: A Vow Forbidding Her All Work
steps.stepSummary: If a husband vows that his wife may not do any work, he must divorce her and pay her כתובה, because idleness drives a person out of her mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Even a man who makes a vow forbidding his wife to do any work must divorce her and pay her כתובה, because idleness leads to madness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds a related rule. Keeping a wife from all work harms her so much that the husband must divorce her and pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'even' shows he agrees that idleness is harmful, and he takes it further. A husband who forbids his wife to do any work is hurting her, since total idleness leads to dullness and madness. So he must free her with her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes a vow forbidding someone something
He must divorce her and pay her כתובה

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה lists the wife's tasks and how maidservants reduce them. רבי אליעזר and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל both stress that total idleness is harmful.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף הַמַּדִּיר אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ מִלַּעֲשׂוֹת מְלָאכָה —
phrases.english: Even one who vows that his wife may not do work
must divorce her and give her the כתובה,
because idleness leads to madness.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר אַף הַמַּדִּיר אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea that idleness is harmful and applies it to a husband's vow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband who vows that his wife may do no work must divorce her and pay her כתובה.

steps.title: Does She Really Grind?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה can say a woman grinds, when grinding is normally done at a mill.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think that she grinds?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה with a question about its wording: 'she grinds.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain was usually ground at large millstones turned by water or animals, not by a woman at home. So the word 'grinds' in the משנה seems wrong. The next lines will offer two ways to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (This can't be right)

phrases.english: GEMARA: Could it enter your mind that she grinds?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's analysis of the משנה's first task.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word טוחנת in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Grinding was normally done at a big mill, not by the woman herself.

steps.title: She Arranges the Grinding
steps.stepSummary: Read the word as מטחנת: she takes care of getting the grain ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: she arranges the grinding.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer changes how we read the word. She does not grind the grain herself; she makes sure it gets ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מטחנת means 'she causes it to be ground.' She brings the grain to the mill and watches that it is ground properly. That way the משנה fits how grinding was actually done.

keyTerms.meaning: She has it ground; she arranges the grinding

phrases.english: Rather, say: she arranges the grinding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 by rereading the word.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה means she grinds the grain with her own hands at the mill.
steps.terutzMaskana: She is responsible for having the grain ground.

steps.title: Or: With a Hand Mill
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: she really does grind herself, using a small hand mill.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: she grinds with a hand mill.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer that keeps the משנה's wording as it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no need to change the word. The משנה is talking about a small hand mill used at home, which a woman can turn herself. So 'she grinds' is meant literally.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (a second answer)

phrases.english: And if you want, say: with a hand mill.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of step 13 without changing the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Grinding must mean the big mill, which a woman doesn't run herself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is talking about a hand mill, so she really does grind herself.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow רבי חייא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה's list of a wife's chores does not fit רבי חייא, who says a wife is only for beauty and children.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה does not follow רבי חייא. He taught that a wife is only for beauty and only for having children, not for housework.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the משנה, which gives a wife household jobs, disagrees with a teaching of רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a wife grinds, bakes, and does other work for her husband. רבי חייא describes a wife's role only in terms of beauty and children, which leaves no room for chores. So the two sources cannot both be right.

keyTerms.meaning: A great teacher of ברייתות from the early generation of אמוראים

phrases.english: Our mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Ḥiyya,
as Rabbi Ḥiyya teaches:
A wife is only for beauty,
a wife is only for children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining how a wife grinds, the גמרא notes that the whole idea of a wife's chores clashes with רבי חייא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's list of a wife's duties does not follow רבי חייא, who sees a wife's role as beauty and children.

steps.title: More teachings of רבי חייא about a wife's beauty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds more teachings of רבי חייא in the same spirit: a wife is for wearing finery, linen beautifies a wife, and certain foods give a daughter a fair complexion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא also taught that a wife is for wearing a woman's jewelry. He taught that a man who wants to make his wife beautiful should dress her in linen. A man who wants his daughter to have fair skin should feed her young chickens and give her milk as she grows up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting רבי חייא's teachings, which all focus on a woman's beauty rather than her work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These extra quotes show that רבי חייא had a consistent theme: caring for a woman's appearance. Nothing new is argued here. The quotes just fill out the picture of his view that was set against the משנה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ḥiyya teaches:
A wife is only for a woman's finery.
And Rabbi Ḥiyya teaches:
One who wants to beautify his wife
should dress her in linen garments.
One who wants to whiten his daughter
phrases.notes: He means giving her a fair, light complexion.

phrases.english: should feed her young chickens
and give her milk to drink close to her time.
phrases.notes: "Her time" here means as she approaches adulthood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more teachings of רבי חייא that share the same theme.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא gives practical advice for a wife's and daughter's beauty: linen clothing, young chickens, and milk.

steps.title: Nursing: does the משנה disagree with בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a wife nurses her child. The גמרא suggests this goes against בית שמאי, who say a woman who vowed not to nurse may stop. בית הלל say the husband can force her to nurse.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said she nurses her son. Should we say the משנה is not like בית שמאי? A ברייתא teaches: if a woman vowed not to nurse her son, בית שמאי say she takes the breast out of his mouth. בית הלל say her husband can force her to nurse him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה, nursing, and suggests the משנה only fits בית הלל and not בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a wife already owes her husband nursing, her vow should not be able to cancel that duty. בית שמאי let the vow take effect, which suggests they think she never had a duty to nurse. That would clash with the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion that may be rejected)
The two great schools of תנאים

phrases.english: "And she nurses her son."
Shall we say our mishna is not in accordance with Beit Shammai?
As it is taught in a baraita:
If she vowed not to nurse her son,
Beit Shammai say:
She pulls the breast out of his mouth.
Beit Hillel say:
He forces her, and she nurses him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the משנה's line about nursing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the משנה's duty to nurse fits every opinion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בית שמאי let a vow cancel nursing, so they seem to hold there is no built-in duty to nurse. That contradicts the משנה.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: a divorced mother
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: after a divorce the husband cannot force her to nurse. But if the baby already recognizes her, he pays her and forces her, because the baby is in danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she was divorced, he cannot force her. But if the baby recognized her, he pays her a wage and forces her, and she nurses him because of the danger to the baby.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא, which adds the case of a divorced mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once divorced, she no longer owes her ex-husband anything, so he cannot normally force her. The exception is a baby who knows his mother and may refuse anyone else. Then she must nurse for pay, to keep the baby safe.

phrases.english: If she was divorced, he cannot force her.
But if he recognized her,
phrases.notes: "He" is the baby, who already knows his mother.

phrases.english: he gives her wages and forces her,
and she nurses him because of the danger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A divorced woman cannot be forced to nurse, unless the baby recognizes her. Then she is paid and must nurse because of the danger.

steps.title: בית שמאי are talking about a vow the husband let stand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה could still follow בית שמאי. Their case is one where the husband upheld her vow. They hold he is the one responsible for it, while בית הלל hold she is responsible.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say the משנה follows בית שמאי, here the ברייתא is dealing with a case where she vowed and he upheld her vow. בית שמאי think he put his finger between her teeth, meaning he caused it. בית הלל think she put her finger between her own teeth, meaning she caused it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the idea that the משנה can fit בית שמאי, by narrowing the ברייתא to a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this answer, בית שמאי agree a wife normally must nurse. They let the vow stand only because the husband chose not to cancel it, so the blame and the loss fall on him. בית הלל say the vow is still her doing, so her duty stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
He upheld (did not cancel) the vow
A finger between her teeth: a picture for who caused the result

steps.confusionAlert: "Finger between her teeth" is not a real action. It is a figure of speech asking who is responsible for the vow staying in force.

phrases.english: Even if you say it follows Beit Shammai,
what are we dealing with here?
A case where she vowed,
and he upheld it for her.
phrases.notes: A husband can cancel some of his wife's vows. Here he chose to leave it in place.

phrases.english: And Beit Shammai hold:
he put a finger between her teeth,
and Beit Hillel hold:
she put a finger between her teeth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion in step 18 by limiting the ברייתא to a vow the husband upheld.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית שמאי hold that a wife has no duty to nurse at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית שמאי agree there is a duty. They only free her because the husband upheld her vow and so took responsibility for it.

steps.title: Then why argue about nursing and not the כתובה in general?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if the real argument is about who is responsible for an upheld vow, they should have argued about it in the general setting of a כתובה, not about nursing in particular.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let them argue about the כתובה in general!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 20 by asking why the argument would be placed specifically on nursing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Who is responsible for an upheld vow is a general question. It matters for many cases, such as whether she loses her כתובה. Putting the argument on nursing suggests it really is about nursing, which weakens the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract and its payment

phrases.english: Then let them argue about a marriage contract in general.
phrases.notes: He means the question of whether she loses her כתובה over a vow her husband upheld.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that בית שמאי's ruling is about an upheld vow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general rule about responsibility for vows would naturally be argued about in general, not tied to nursing.

steps.title: A ברייתא says outright that בית שמאי free her from nursing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second problem: another ברייתא quotes בית שמאי plainly saying a woman does not nurse, with no vow mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, a ברייתא teaches: בית שמאי say she does not nurse!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, stronger challenge against the answer from step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא says nothing about a vow. It shows that בית שמאי simply hold a woman has no duty to nurse. That directly clashes with the משנה.

phrases.english: And furthermore:
it is taught in a baraita: Beit Shammai say:
She does not nurse!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection to the answer in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בית שמאי agree a wife must nurse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quotes בית שמאי directly, with no vow involved, saying she does not nurse.

steps.title: Conclusion: the משנה is not like בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the משנה's rule that a wife nurses clearly does not follow בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear: our משנה is not like בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the attempt to fit the משנה with בית שמאי and accepts the original suggestion from step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After both challenges, the answer from step 20 cannot stand. The משנה, which makes nursing a wife's duty, follows בית הלל.
steps.whatToRemember: A wife's duty to nurse her child follows בית הלל. בית שמאי hold she does not have to nurse. רבי חייא, who sees a wife as being for beauty and children, also does not match the משנה's list of chores.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear:
our mishna is not in accordance with Beit Shammai.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מְחַוַּורְתָּא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenges and goes back to the suggestion from step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's rule that a wife nurses her child follows בית הלל, not בית שמאי.

steps.title: Quoting the phrase 'if the baby recognized her'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the words 'if he recognized her' from the earlier ברייתא, so it can examine them next.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: if the baby recognized her (the husband pays her and forces her to keep nursing even after the divorce).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes a short phrase from the ברייתא in Step 19 so it can now discuss that phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 20-23 dealt with whether the משנה follows בית שמאי. Now the גמרא returns to one detail of the ברייתא: the case where the baby already recognizes its mother. In that case a divorced woman can be forced to nurse because the baby is in danger. Quoting the words prepares a question about what counts as 'recognizing.'

keyTerms.meaning: Recognition: the baby knows its own mother and will not easily accept another nurse

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new ruling. The גמרא is just repeating words from the ברייתא in Step 19 to start talking about them.

phrases.english: If he recognized her.
phrases.notes: He means the baby. These words come from the ברייתא in Step 19: once the baby knows her, she can be forced to keep nursing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After concluding in Step 23 that the משנה does not follow בית שמאי, the גמרא goes back to the ברייתא of Step 19 and quotes its phrase about the baby recognizing its mother.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quoted phrase: if the baby recognizes its mother, the divorced mother can be paid and forced to keep nursing. The phrase is quoted here so the גמרא can define 'recognizing.'
